text:
priya: Quick sanity check — Orpheus-9B int4 shows a ~6.8% drop on the longform benchmark (>=1024 tokens), but token cost is down ~2.2x vs int8. Can we surface signal parity and decide routing? :thinking:
mateo: Thanks — what's the slice? multi-turn dialogue or single-turn generation?
priya: Multi-turn, average 1.2k tokens/session. Regression concentrated in coherence/long-range factuality slices.
chen: Do we have priming / KV-cache warmstart differences? int4 KV eviction pattern could amplify errors on long prefixes.
omar: I ran a quick diff on logits for a failing example — top-5 shifts mostly after token 450. Looks like attention scaling subtly diverges.
neil: Any perf tail impact? What's latency delta at p95 for our standard 8GB batch?
priya: p95 is ~12% faster on int4; p99 mostly comparable but tails slightly noisier under heavy concurrency.
omeanops-bot: deploy-notify: Canary build 2026.03.20-orpheus-int4 pushed to dedicated test cluster.
mateo: For GTN/product guidance: if quality delta confined to >512 tokens, recommend routing policy: use int8 for sessions >512 or when coherence score <threshold.
chen: Agree. Also try a mixed-precision fallback that keeps KV-cache in int8 for prefixes >512. Might keep runtime benefits but reduce divergence.
omar: Quick experiment config I ran:
```
model_variant: orpheus-9b
quant: int4
kv_cache_dtype: float16  # baseline
hybrid_kv: int8_for_prefix=true
routing_threshold_tokens: 512
```
Result: coherence metric improved from -6.8% -> -2.1% regression.
neil: Cost math — current per-token infra cost (int8) = $0.0000045/token. int4 run is ~2.2x cheaper -> $0.00000205/token. If we route long sessions to int8, net cost increase depends on fraction of traffic >512. What's our traffic split?
priya: On staging traffic sample, ~18% of sessions exceed 512 tokens. If we keep 82% on int4 and 18% on int8, expected weighted unit cost = 0.82*0.00000205 + 0.18*0.0000045 = ~$0.0000025/token (rough).
mateo: Product tradeoff: 18% cost bump to preserve long-form quality on critical flows seems reasonable. For GTN messaging: recommend "hybrid routing by session length + KV hybridization" as the default for Orpheus-9B.
chen: We should also run a small user-facing A/B with quality evals on 5k long sessions — measure retention of factuality and instruction follow-through.
priya: Agree. Proposal for rollout:
- Start canary 5% traffic with hybrid_kv enabled and length-based routing
- Monitor quality signals (bleu/ROUGE proxies + our hallucination classifier) and latency/cost
- If OK after 48h, ramp to 30% then 100% with a fallback to orpheus-9b-int8 if regression >3% on any critical slice
mateo: Sounds good. For dev docs / ops we need a short playbook entry for routing flags and how to flip hybrid_kv. Priya can you draft?
priya: Will draft now. Quick snippet to add to playbook for ops:
```
# launch params
--routing.policy.length_threshold=512
--model.variant.orpheus-9b.int4.hybrid_kv=true
--fallback.model=orpheus-9b-int8
--canary.percent=5
```
omar: One more thing — queueing/batching can interact badly with hybrid KV. Add `batch_compat=true` check in rollout to avoid token misalignment.
neil: On econ comms to GTN: we should show the per-session delta and the expected unit econ with hybrid routing. I can assemble a 1-slide calc: baseline int8 vs hybrid weighted vs pure int4 worst-case.
priya: Action items:
- priya: draft ops playbook + canary config (today)
- chen: run 5k long-session QA A/B (24h)
- mateo: prepare GTN note + unit-econ slide (today)
- omar: add batch_compat check in canary (now)
- neil: run final cost sims and put numbers in slide (today)
If all green, we ship hybrid routing as default for Orpheus-9B.
mateo: :thumbsup: Let's aim to have the canary up by EOD.
priya: I'll post the playbook link when done. Thank you all.
